chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the purchase of palm trees, and he said: 'My father (peace be upon him) disliked the purchase of palm trees before the fruit of the year emerges, but for two or three years he would say: "If it does not bear fruit in this year, it will bear fruit in the next year."'

Ya'qub said: And I asked him about a man who buys palm trees and fruit before they emerge, purchasing for two years, or three years, or four. He said: 'There is no harm. Only the purchase of one year before the fruit emerges is disliked, out of fear of defect until it becomes clear.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on purchasing palm trees before their fruit is visible?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions by contrasting the Imam’s general dislike for single-year palm purchases with the permissibility of multi-year contracts. It highlights the practical jurisprudence of risk mitigation, where the potential loss in one year is offset by the certainty of harvest in subsequent years, reflecting the Imams' nuanced approach to agricultural economics.
